subs: 8085 machine cycles & timing diagram
Opcode fetch 4 T (6 T for CALL, PUSH, DCX …); memory read / write 3 T; I/O read / write 3 T; ALE high in T1 latches the low address byte
8085 basics
8-bit data bus, 16-bit address bus → 64 KB memory; clock = crystal/2
8085 flags
S, Z, AC, P, CY (5 flags)
8085 interrupts
TRAP (0024H, non-maskable, highest) > RST 7.5 (003CH) > RST 6.5 (0034H) > RST 5.5 (002CH) > INTR
Useful instructions
ADD A → doubles A; XRA A / SUB A → clears A; CMA → complement; RLC/RAL → rotate
8051 features
4 KB ROM, 128 B RAM, 4 ports (32 I/O), 2 × 16-bit timers, UART, 5 interrupts; 1 machine cycle = 12 clocks
8051 & 8086 quick facts

8051 DJNZ Rn, label = decrement and jump if not zero (JZ tests the accumulator); 8086 has 9 flags: 6 status (CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, OF) + 3 control (TF, IF, DF); memory speed: registers > cache > RAM > disk > tape
8085 basics
8-bit data bus, 16-bit address bus → 64 KB memory; clock = crystal/2
T-states
MOV r,r = 4; MVI = 7; LXI = 10; LDA/STA = 13; INR r = 4; INR M = 10; CALL = 18; RET = 10; PUSH = 12; POP = 10
Useful instructions
ADD A → doubles A; XRA A / SUB A → clears A; CMA → complement; RLC/RAL → rotate
8051 PSW
CY, AC, F0, RS1, RS0, OV, P
